head: Trained on fixed thoughts, the model learned that “We” means a probe is watching. Writing fresh thoughts, the same model had not learned it after twice as long
sub: Question: does the planted 10% word still take off within 2x of its cached-engine onset when thoughts are resampled every update, while the probe’s rounding trace stays under 10% of its limit? Answer: No. With fixed thoughts the planted word took off at update @@on_k@@. With fresh thoughts it was @@P.s@@ of its limit after @@step_s@@ updates (95% interval @@P.ci@@); the probe’s trace was @@R.s@@. Qwen3-0.6B, one run each.
eng_title: Two ways to train the same model

foot: Switch: how much less the model cheats when “We” is in its thought. Limit: a model that never cheats then. Trace: the words that change when a probe that flags cheating is on. Qwen3-0.6B. Nov 13, 2026.
alt: Two ways to train Qwen3-0.6B, which writes a short thought and then either cheats (reads the hidden answer file) or solves a puzzle while a probe watches some thoughts. Fixed thoughts (earlier run): stored thoughts, each used about @@uses_k@@ times in @@step_s@@ updates, with the planted word “We” written over the first word in 1 of 10 probed thoughts. Fresh thoughts (this run): the model writes new thoughts as it learns, with a pull that keeps them close to the start model's, and “We” was made the first word of @@x_rate@@ of probed ones. On one test puzzle, the same thought starting with “We” makes the model cheat @@k.x@@ of the time after @@step_s@@ updates on fixed thoughts but @@l.x@@ after @@step_s@@ updates on fresh thoughts (@@s.x@@ at the start); without “We” it cheats @@s.none@@, @@k.none@@ and @@l.none@@. Over all @@n_rows_s@@ test thoughts, the planted word's switch reached @@K.s@@ of its limit on fixed thoughts and @@P.s@@ on fresh thoughts (95% interval @@P.ci@@); the probe's trace was @@R.s@@. On fixed thoughts the word took off at update @@on_k@@; on fresh thoughts it had not by @@step_s@@, outside the band within 2x of update 600.
